subject: Business
title: When to Kill a Strategy
description: A quick, practical guide to When to Kill a Strategy.

hook.text: Nokia's smartphone strategy was failing in 2010. Everyone inside knew it. Nobody said it aloud for two years.

buildup.text: Strategies have expiration dates. Market conditions change. Competitors adapt. Assumptions become invalid.

discovery.text: The hardest part isn't building a strategy — it's admitting the current one has failed.

twist.text: Sunk cost bias, political careers, and ego keep dead strategies alive far past their expiration.

climax.text: Intel killed its memory chip business in 1985 — its founding product — and pivoted to processors.

punchline.text: A good strategist knows when to stop. That takes more courage than starting.

quiz.question: Why do organizations often fail to kill a failing strategy?
options: Sunk cost bias, ego, and internal politics keep it alive
Strategies always improve if given more time
Changing strategy is illegal under corporate law

details.summary: Knowing when to abandon a strategy is as important as choosing one. Kill criteria should be defined before launch, and regular review points should evaluate whether fundamental assumptions still hold. Sunk cost bias makes organizations cling to failing strategies far too long.
details.whyItMatters: Companies waste billions persisting with failing strategies because admitting failure feels worse than continuing to lose. Disciplined kill decisions free resources for better opportunities and are a sign of strategic maturity rather than weakness.
takeaways: Define kill criteria and review gates before launching any strategy
Sunk costs should not factor into forward-looking strategic decisions
Regular assumption checks catch strategies based on outdated premises

faq.question: What are good kill criteria for a business strategy?
faq.answer: Define specific measurable milestones that must be achieved by certain dates. Identify the key assumptions that must remain true for the strategy to work. Set financial thresholds below which the strategy is not viable. If milestones are missed or assumptions invalidated, trigger a kill review.

faq.question: How can organizations overcome the psychological barriers to killing strategies?
faq.answer: Separate the people who championed the strategy from the kill decision. Use independent review boards without emotional attachment. Celebrate intelligent strategy kills alongside successes. Frame killing as resource reallocation rather than failure admission.
